analysis: The PR changes one documentation line in docs/architecture/inference.md (line 1846, the `stop` row of the sampling-translation table). It describes scoped stop-string matching: GPT-OSS Harmony final-message scope via ModelEOSPolicy.stopStringScope, per-request reasoning/tool-call span exclusion for Gemma 4 and think parsers (ReasoningStopScope), and whole-output matching for the native block engine. The changed line is outside the two supplied base units (starting at 2428 and 2761), so I examined the surrounding base text, which is unchanged context, against the threat model. The edit is documentation only and changes no code, so it adds no control, weakens none, and does not alter trust boundaries. The revised text could affect consumer-visible output semantics (T-007, TB-007). The stop-scope behavior itself is unverified because no source was supplied for StopHoldback, ReasoningStopScope or ModelEOSPolicy. Stop scoping affects only which generated text ends a response. It does not touch the sealed prompt/response path (A-001), the prefix cache and its T-041 posture, attestation, or the add-on and installer boundaries. Neither the doc line nor the surrounding Flint, MiMo or GLM text mentions plaintext logging or new storage. Integration should confirm that the unreviewed code implementing the scoped stop matching exists and does not change the content-free logging or encryption behavior. This documentation change itself raises no concrete security regression.
